q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026. Today is August 16, 2026.
**Time remaining: ~10 days**

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release. This means the guidance they provide for Q3 FY2027 (the next quarter), NOT their actual Q2 FY2027 results.

Based on the research provided:
- NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 guidance was $91.0 billion ±2% (i.e., $89.18B-$92.82B range)
- UBS predicts NVIDIA will provide Q3 FY2027 guidance of approximately **$107-108 billion**
- The rationale: steady Blackwell demand and faster-than-expected Rubin platform ramp-up

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA's forward guidance (for Q3 FY2027) will fall in the **$105-110 billion range**, with a point estimate around **$107-108 billion** based on UBS analysis. This represents significant sequential growth from the Q1 guidance of $91B, consistent with accelerating AI demand.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Weaker-than-expected Blackwell demand** in the current quarter
- **Supply chain constraints** or manufacturing delays for next-gen products
- **Macro weakness** or customer pullback on capex spending
- **China restrictions tightening** further, impacting revenue opportunities
- **Competitive pressures** from AMD or other alternatives gaining share
- UBS estimate being overly bullish relative to actual Q2 results

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Better-than-expected Blackwell ramp** continuing into Q3
- **Accelerated Rubin adoption** (UBS suggests 500K GPU/month trajectory)
- **Data center capex cycle** stronger than consensus expects
- **China revenue inclusion** if policy changes
- **Market share gains** vs. competitors
- Strong enough demand to raise guidance beyond UBS expectations

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research explicitly provides:
- Q1 FY2027 guidance: $91.0B ±2%
- UBS Q3 FY2027 forecast: $107-108B

This represents ~18% sequential growth Q1→Q3, which is plausible for NVIDIA given the AI cycle dynamics and product transitions. There is no historical base rate provided in the materials, but the guidance trajectory shown is consistent with NVIDIA's recent growth pattern.

## Reasoning on the range

The given range is $99.5B-$115.5B. The midpoint is ~$107.5B, which aligns almost exactly with the UBS guidance estimate of $107-108B. This suggests:
- The range was deliberately constructed around analyst consensus
- My estimate should anchor heavily on the UBS forecast
- The lower and upper bounds allow for meaningful variance around this point

The UBS estimate of $107-108B is from a reputable source (clearly cited) and is based on specific supply/demand dynamics (Blackwell, Rubin). With only 10 days until the earnings call, major surprises are unlikely unless Q2 results dramatically miss expectations.

## Final probability distribution

Given the UBS guidance of $107-108B and the proximity to the earnings release (where most information is now likely locked in):

Low (10th percentile): 103000000000
Median (50th percentile): 107500000000
High (90th percentile): 112000000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA will release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026, covering the period ending July 26, 2026 [aliteq.com](https://aliteq.com/nvidia-q2-fy27-earnings-preview-ubs-2026). The company's own guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, as announced on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/) [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm) [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/) [barchart.com](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3449043/what-to-expect-from-nvidia-s-q2-2027-earnings-report). This outlook does not include any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/) [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).

UBS, however, predicts NVIDIA will report $94-95 billion for Q2 FY2027, exceeding the company's guidance, and will provide an October-quarter (Q3 FY2027) guide of roughly $107-108 billion [aliteq.com](https://aliteq.com/nvidia-q2-fy27-earnings-preview-ubs-2026). This higher estimate is attributed to steady Blackwell demand and an unexpectedly fast ramp-up of the next-gen Rubin platform, which UBS forecasts could reach 500,000 GPU shipments a month [aliteq.com](https://aliteq.com/nvidia-q2-fy27-earnings-preview-ubs-2026).
